correctness.rationale: Complete radius-one binary Hamming balls intersect iff center distance is at most two. Distinct Dyck centers have equal weight and hence even distance, so disjoint-ball packings are exactly distance-at-least-four codes. Independently enumerated sources by the equivalent zero-based up-step position bounds p_i <= 2i, rebuilt all balls including unaltered outputs and non-Dyck outputs, checked the integer witnesses, and verified both sparse rational LP certificates by every primal and dual inequality. The (source count, integer witness size, matching primal/dual objective) triples were (1,1,1),(2,1,1),(5,2,2),(14,4,4),(42,10,10),(132,22,26). In the sixth case there were 726 outputs, with 68 nonzero primal weights and 51 nonzero dual weights. For the crucial separate integer upper bound, a fresh bitmask decision search on the graph formed by literal disjoint balls found a 22-clique after 8716 calls and excluded a 23-clique after 137602 calls. Each reverse traversal uses the proper coloring of its remaining prefix, so the prefix color count bounds a clique extension and the skipped branches cannot attain the target. For n <= 5 the LP upper bounds already match the integer witnesses. Thus the first gap is 26-22=4 and the ratio is 13/11. The frozen C++ prefix-color logic was also inspected; neither its recorded node count nor the optional MILP result was used as evidence of the upper bound.
residual_risks: The finite six-instance proof says nothing about larger semilengths or the LP with a different received alphabet.

value.rationale: The complete ball-packing LP is the natural relaxation for unrestricted binary one-bit substitution on this structured balanced language. Determining the first instance where it overestimates the integer code size by four, including after rounding, gives a concrete limit on using that bound to certify optimality. The earlier exact equality range is part of that boundary claim rather than an arbitrary cutoff.
residual_risks: This is a finite diagnostic for this relaxation; it establishes neither an asymptotic gap nor a general Dyck-code method.
